name: Breezeborne Refrain
desc: A dark green bow string made out of pure and flawless gemstone. It never fails to summon a warm spring breeze whenever it is drawn.

materials.desc: Common currency. The one language everybody speaks.

materials.name: The Frost Emperor's Revival
materials.desc:
Weapon Ascension Material.
The hero who emerged from the snowfields had yet to become the ruler of that frozen realm, but even then, he had already shown a habit of confiding far too much to those around him.
So he was all the more surprised when he received a gift from the fae of snow, who at the time had not yet taken their human form.
As far as he knew, he never told them that he was born from an egg as pale as ice deep within the wing-like mountains, nor did he ever mention the date of his birth.

materials.name: Accreted Fragment
materials.desc:
An accretion formed by powerful Volkodlak.
An accretion that has only just begun to attach to an internal organ or bone. As the Volkodlak's power grows, it may eventually cover an entire region of the body, or a whole organ.

materials.name: Chimeric Core
materials.desc:
The internal core harvested from aberrant man-made monsters.
This is the most fundamental core grown within a man-made monster. Yet, simple as it may be, it contains the primordial design for the growth of all man-made creations.

materials.name: Mora
materials.desc: Common currency. The one language everybody speaks.

materials.name: The Frost Emperor's Ceremony
materials.desc:
Weapon Ascension Material.
The fae of the court didn't understand why a gift meant for the Tsar must be made in such shape. They knew only to lavish their craft upon ornaments bright as jewels.
Only the Tsar seated upon the throne and the fae of snow understood the meaning behind it.
For what mattered was never the ceremony, but the ancient truth it preserved.

An accretion that has clung to an internal organ or bone for a long time. Once removed, such accretions are regarded as symbols of power and carefully preserved by the creature's descendants.

materials.desc:
The internal core harvested from aberrant man-made monsters.
A relatively complex core harvested from a man-made monster. This symbiotic nucleus is engineered to sustain the biological cycles of two distinct life-forms, seamlessly weaving them into a single organism.

materials.desc:
Weapon Ascension Material.
On the night the truth stirred like bitter waves, she prepared this gift for her friend upon the throne—though she herself was no longer the person she used to be.
They both seemed to understand that they might never speak to each other like this again.
For after that night, the path they once walked together diverged—sundered by the weakness of one, and the fury of the other.

An accretion formed by powerful Volkodlak.
An accretion that has fully fused with an organ or bone. One could even say it's a newly grown bone or organ at the nodes of the Volkodlak's power circulation. Only long-lived Volkodlaks who have ceaselessly honed their strength can form such growths within their bodies.

materials.name: Prime Chimeric Nexus
materials.desc:
The internal core harvested from aberrant man-made monsters.
The most complex core a man-made monster can possibly sustain, serving as an artificially engineered yet flawless seed of life. Whoever brought this creation into life has surely unlocked the very secrets of how life itself is shaped.

materials.name: The Frost Emperor's Farewell
materials.desc:
Weapon Ascension Material.
An object that appeared upon the table on the eve of war, though none knew when or how it'd come to be there.
He recognized it for the handiwork of the friend he hadn't seen for many long years.
Only then did he realize, that this was the beginning of every calamity, the bitter fruit of every desire, and the omen of every destruction.

value.text: Increases Energy Recharge by <color=#36ffff>20%/25%/30%/35%/40%</color> . When the equipping character hits the opponent with their Elemental Skill or Elemental Burst, they gain a stack of "Hymn of the Pure." This effect can trigger once every 0.03s, max 3 stacks, and at 3 stacks, all instances of "Hymn of the Pure" are cleared to give the equipping character "Thus Lied the Viper" instead. This grants nearby party members a <color=#36ffff>24%/30%/36%/42%/48%</color> Stellar Glimmer reaction DMG boost for 12s, during which no stacks of "Hymn of the Pure" can be obtained. The aforementioned effects can still trigger even when the equipping character is not on the field.

customize.name: Beyond the Chrysalis
customize.desc: A longsword brimming with light and color, and as weightless as a butterfly when brandished. It was once used by a certain individual to break bonds.

customize.name: Hymn of the Maelstrom
customize.desc: An exquisite lamp crafted out of blue chalcedony which looks like a treasure right out of a fairy tale. It is said that a song of praise, forgotten by all, slumbers sealed inside this lamp.

customize.name: Breezeborne Refrain
customize.desc: A dark green bow string made out of pure and flawless gemstone. It never fails to summon a warm spring breeze whenever it is drawn.

customize.name: New Bough
customize.desc: A sword made from sacred wood, said to have once turned the tide of battle.

customize.name: Winter's Heavy Heart
customize.desc: A ceremonial artifact formed from the purest ice and snow. Legend has it that generations of Snegovik lords used it in coronation ceremonies until five hundred years ago.

customize.name: Dragon's Bane
customize.desc: A polearm decorated with an entwining golden dragon. Light and sharp, this weapon may very well kill dragons with ease.

customize.name: Favonius Greatsword
customize.desc: A heavy ceremonial sword of the Knights of Favonius. It channels elemental power easily and is highly destructive.

desc.text:
In the years before the holy torch of the Pale Star was lit, the Silver Court of Veneter had been a haven of renown equal to Kitezhgrad.
Fae from various clans praised the Lady of the Vila merciful ways, hailing her a saint who had banished the bitter cold and soothed their pain.
Indeed, though war raged and blood stained the frozen rivers, Vaselisa von Strivozha was never the enemy of any.
Pure, benevolent, and true. So countless songs of later ages would praise her, as gentle and warm as the soft breeze of spring.
And so it was that, on a bitter night cold as frost and snow, a noble with nowhere left to turn came knocking at the splendid gates of Veneter.
He was a war hero who had served the Blood-Devourer, a renowned commander who had routed the armies of the Pale Star in battle time and again.
Yet, for speaking plainly against his brutal liege, for urging him not to slaughter the Water Imps who were still his allies, he had been stripped of every title and office.
His wife and children had been subjected to the ultimate penalty of the Blood Eagle, while the people who paid him tribute were brutally plundered and murdered by his liege's own guards, leaving the fields strewn with corpses.
He had come knocking at the gates of Veneter, asking only that the merciful saint pave the way and grant him an audience with the young Tsar so he might submit himself to the latter.
The saint of Veneter listened quietly to his tale, and soon tears of pity glimmered in her jade-green eyes.
"Alrekr Jarizleivich, my good man, my gallant hero... How could I not weep for those who have died unjustly?
Bring the surviving people under your care, the weary and impoverished with nowhere else to go, those who have suffered so grievously, all to my lands.
My estate shall always keep its gates open to every soul battered by hardship, and you... may you find rest here as well."
The beauteous saint, famed for her mastery of perfumery, personally filled a cup with fragrant warming mead for her weary guest, then knelt to remove the old commander's boots...
...And as the golden drink caught in his throat the metal of his blood, she calmly drew the sorrow from her eyes.
Before dawn had even broken, a secret powerful enough to turn the tides of war had already been carried by the wind to the table of the king of the Volkodlak.
Days later, a coffin draped in red and white silk was placed upon a sled and escorted by attendants to the royal court of the Pale Star.
The saint of Veneter walked beside it herself, then fell before the young Emperor Monomakh, weeping inconsolably.
Grief had left her without words. No lament was sung; only tears fell like pearls, soaking her white robes.
Glowatza, who was at the time still a maidservant, bowed her head in mourning before the Tsar. Her voice trembled as she recounted the Volkodlak's savagery.
"Though my mistress had taken the survivors into her care, she could not prevent the Blood-Devourer's spies from poisoning the valiant general...
Now, only Your Majesty's mercy can save the countless weeping souls upon this cold and desolate land."
Through the veil of her tears, she saw in the youth's sky-blue eyes a hatred both righteous and compassionate.
Indeed. Let the noblest of angers surge like a great wave, let order clash against order, steel against steel,
While the wind remains forever the wind: gentle, elusive, and free, formless and ever-changing, never bound by delusion.
...
The carriage on the journey home rolled through the deep snows that had lain unmelted since time immemorial. The saint brushed away the glistening tear at the corner of her eye, and turned her gaze upon her somber attendant.
"Photius, you may as well speak plainly. There is no need to wear such a look all the time. Say what it is that displeases you."
The young Vila, who had been chosen for her service for his skill in preparing elixirs, hurriedly lowered his eyes as he tried desperately to hide the thoughts that had just crossed his mind.
"No... Your judgment has ever seen through what lies hidden. How could one as foolish and lowly as I dare show the slightest disrespect toward your wisdom..."
Her words were greeted by a tinkling laugh.
"There you go again, Photius. You place such faith in those you deem wise that you would sooner persuade yourself to stop thinking.
You worry that the Pale Star King will learn the truth, and you question what I have done. These are all perfectly good questions.
But he will suspect nothing. Indeed, I shall even pretend to trust in his mercy. What reason has he to doubt my tears?
On the one hand, the king of the Volkodlak would have the wind become a blade that cleaves bone. On the other, the Emperor of the Pale Star would have it become a holy sword to cleanse all that is corrupt.
Yet in the end, they both wish the wind to bend to their will, to follow the banners of the mighty and blow where they would have it go.
But Photius, the wind belongs to no one. So long as it continues to blow, none can know where it will carry itself."
The saint of Veneter let her gentle smile fade, her jade-green pupils reflecting the youth's still-innocent face.
"Best you learn from Glowatza. Pride and vanity are poisons that only bring ruin to a clan. Only the gentle wind can blow on forever."
